title: Olivia and the Stubborn Cart
subtitle: Things keep doing what they were doing
author: Olivia's Shelf
blurb: Olivia pushes a little cart and learns that a force is a push or a pull — and that moving things want to keep moving.

magic.launch: The little rocket pushed the air, and the air pushed back.
magic.drop: Everything falls. That pull has a name: gravity.

grok.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

openai.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

pages.heading: It wanted to keep going
pages.text: {Olivia} pushed a little {cart} across the {workshop} floor. It rolled. Then it wanted to keep rolling.

pages.heading: A push or a pull
pages.text: "A {force} is a push or a {pull}," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "No force, and a still cart stays still."

pages.heading: Stubborn motion
pages.text: "A moving cart keeps {moving} until something slows it," said Elon. "That stubbornness is called {inertia}."

pages.heading: Heavy is harder
pages.text: A heavier cart was harder to start. Harder to {stop} too. "More stuff means more stubborn," said {Elon:elon/teach}.

pages.heading: Push back
pages.text: The little {rocket:rocket/whoosh} pushed air backward. The air pushed the rocket {forward}. "Every push has a push back," said Elon.

pages.heading: Keep asking why
pages.text: "Why do I lean when the cart stops?" asked {Olivia:olivia/ask}. "Your body wanted to keep going," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "Ask why again tomorrow."

end.heading: The End
end.text: A force is a push or a pull. Things keep doing what they were doing until a force changes them.
end.prompt: What would you roll, then stop, tomorrow?

credits: Painted for Olivia's Shelf. Elon is a picture-book inventor who teaches physics; this is not a biography.
